prompt: A dataset preserves KD, Ki and IC50 values separately for EGFR–inhibitor pairs and does not pool them. Explain why these measurement types must not be treated as interchangeable.
completion: KD is a thermodynamic binding-dissociation constant (equilibrium affinity of the ligand for the protein). Ki is an inhibition constant derived from enzyme-kinetic models, also an affinity-type constant but assay/model-dependent. IC50 is the concentration giving 50% inhibition under specific assay conditions and depends on substrate/ATP concentration, enzyme amount and incubation time. Because IC50 shifts with assay conditions (e.g., ATP concentration) and, for covalent inhibitors, with preincubation time, pooling KD/Ki/IC50 into one regression target conflates different physical quantities and biases the labels. They are therefore kept separate; only compatible IC50 values are used for the Boltz affinity target.

prompt: For BLU-945 against wild-type EGFR, the biochemical IC50 is 86.0 nM at Km,ATP but 1490 nM at 1 mmol/L ATP (Melis 2026). Explain why the two values differ and the implication for comparing inhibitors.
completion: BLU-945 is ATP-competitive-sensitive: raising ATP from Km to 1 mmol/L increases apparent IC50 (86.0->1490 nM) because ATP competes with the inhibitor for the binding pocket. IC50 is therefore condition-dependent; inhibitors must be compared at matched ATP concentrations, and absolute IC50 values from different assay conditions should not be mixed in a single label set.
